name: geography_set4_p1
label: Geography: set 4 (Sierra Leone's economy, West Africa, Africa, ECOWAS and practical geography)

papers.title: Economic Geography of Sierra Leone: practice set 1
papers.description: 5 original WASSCE-style objective questions on economic geography of sierra leone, each with an explanation and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Cocoa and coffee in Sierra Leone are grown mainly in
questions.explanation:
The forest soils and heavy rainfall of the east suit cocoa and coffee.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the Freetown Peninsula: The Peninsula is mostly urban and forested hills.
- the dry savanna of Koinadugu: Cocoa needs heavy rain and forest soils.
- the mangrove swamps of the coast: Mangrove swamps are salty and waterlogged.

options.label: A
options.content: the east, in Kailahun, Kenema and Kono districts

options.label: D
options.content: the mangrove swamps of the coast

questions.stem: An advantage of swamp rice over upland rice in Sierra Leone is that swamp rice
questions.explanation:
Swamps and bolilands keep their fertility and, with water control, can give two crops a year.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- needs no water: Swamp rice depends on water from rivers, floods or tides.
- is grown only on steep slopes: Upland rice is grown on slopes.
- requires the land to be cleared by burning every year: That describes upland bush fallowing.

options.label: B
options.content: gives higher yields and the soil stays fertile

options.label: C
options.content: is grown only on steep slopes

options.label: D
options.content: requires the land to be cleared by burning every year

questions.stem: N'Dama cattle are reared in northern Sierra Leone because they
questions.explanation:
Tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness, which kills many other breeds.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- give the most milk of any breed: They are kept for their tolerance, not high milk yield.
- need no grazing land: All cattle need pasture.
- were brought from Europe: N'Dama is a West African breed.

options.label: A
options.content: give the most milk of any breed

questions.stem: The sector that earns most of Sierra Leone's export revenue is
questions.explanation:
Iron ore, diamonds, rutile, bauxite and gold provide most export earnings.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- agriculture: Agriculture employs most people but earns less export revenue.
- manufacturing: Manufacturing is small and serves mainly the home market.
- tourism: Tourism is still small.

questions.stem: The Wellington Industrial Estate is located in
questions.explanation:
Most of Sierra Leone's factories are in Freetown, near the port, market, power and labour.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Bo: Bo is a commercial centre in the south.
- Makeni: Makeni is the main town of the north.
- Koidu: Koidu is a mining town in Kono.

papers.title: Geography of West Africa: practice set 1
papers.description: 5 original WASSCE-style objective questions on geography of west africa, each with an explanation and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Which of the following West African countries is landlocked?
questions.explanation:
Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger are the landlocked countries of West Africa.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Ghana: Ghana has a coast on the Gulf of Guinea.
- Togo: Togo has a short coast on the Gulf of Guinea.
- The Gambia: The Gambia has an Atlantic coast at Banjul.

questions.stem: The River Niger rises in
questions.explanation:
The Niger rises in the Guinea Highlands close to the Sierra Leone border and flows north-east before turning south.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the Jos Plateau: The Jos Plateau is in Nigeria, far downstream.
- the Aïr Mountains: The Aïr Mountains are in the Sahara in northern Niger.
- the Atlas Mountains: The Atlas Mountains are in north-west Africa.

questions.stem: The Rivers Niger and Benue meet at
questions.explanation:
The Benue joins the Niger at Lokoja in central Nigeria.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Timbuktu: Timbuktu is on the Niger bend in Mali.
- Kainji: Kainji is a dam upstream on the Niger.
- Lagos: Lagos is on the coast, not on the Niger.

questions.stem: In July, the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) over West Africa lies at about
questions.explanation:
The ITCZ follows the overhead sun north, reaching about 18–20°N in July and August.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- about 5 degrees north: That is near its January position.
- the Equator: The ITCZ moves north of the Equator over West Africa in July.
- about 30 degrees north: That is north of the Sahel, beyond the ITCZ's range.

questions.stem: Groundnuts and cotton are grown mainly in the
questions.explanation:
The Sudan savanna of northern Nigeria and Senegal has a short rainy season suited to groundnuts and cotton.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- tropical rainforest: The forest is too wet; it suits cocoa and oil palm.
- mangrove swamp: Mangrove swamps are salty and waterlogged.
- Sahara desert: The desert is too dry without irrigation.

papers.title: Geography of Africa: practice set 1
papers.description: 5 original WASSCE-style objective questions on geography of africa, each with an explanation and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The highest mountain in Africa is
questions.explanation:
Kilimanjaro in Tanzania rises to 5,895 m.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Mount Kenya: Mount Kenya (5,199 m) is the second highest.
- Mount Cameroon: Mount Cameroon is much lower.
- Toubkal: Toubkal (4,167 m) is the highest peak of the Atlas.

questions.stem: The longest river in Africa is the
questions.explanation:
The Nile is about 6,650 km long and flows north into the Mediterranean.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Congo: The Congo is the second longest and carries the most water.
- Niger: The Niger is the third longest.
- Zambezi: The Zambezi is much shorter.

questions.stem: The Great Rift Valley of East Africa was formed by
questions.explanation:
Tension pulled the crust apart and a block sank between parallel faults.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- river erosion over millions of years: Rivers did not carve the Rift Valley.
- folding of rock layers: Folding forms fold mountains.
- glacial erosion: Glaciers did not form it.

options.label: A
options.content: river erosion over millions of years

options.label: B
options.content: faulting, as land sank between parallel faults

questions.stem: The largest lake in Africa is
questions.explanation:
Lake Victoria is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania and is the source of the White Nile.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Lake Chad: Lake Chad is shallow and shrinking.
- Lake Volta: Lake Volta is a man-made reservoir.
- Lake Malawi: Lake Malawi is smaller than Lake Victoria.

questions.stem: The Mediterranean climate in Africa is found in
questions.explanation:
Mediterranean climates lie at the northern and southern tips of the continent, about 30–37° from the Equator.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the Congo Basin: The Congo Basin has an equatorial climate.
- the Sahel: The Sahel is semi-arid.
- the East African highlands: These have a cool highland climate.

options.label: D
options.content: the far north-west and the far south-west (the Cape)

papers.title: ECOWAS and Regional Cooperation: practice set 1
papers.description: 5 original WASSCE-style objective questions on ecowas and regional cooperation, each with an explanation and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: ECOWAS was established in
questions.explanation:
The Treaty of Lagos was signed on 28 May 1975.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 1963: 1963 is when the OAU was founded.
- 1993: 1993 is when the ECOWAS treaty was revised.
- 1973: 1973 is when the Mano River Union was founded.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the ECOWAS Commission is in
questions.explanation:
The ECOWAS Commission, Parliament and Court of Justice are in Abuja, Nigeria.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Lagos: The treaty was signed in Lagos, but the Commission is in Abuja.
- Freetown: Freetown is the headquarters of the Mano River Union.
- Accra: Accra hosts the AfCFTA secretariat.

questions.stem: ECOMOG is
questions.explanation:
ECOMOG intervened in Liberia and Sierra Leone, where it helped restore the elected government in 1998.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the ECOWAS development bank: The bank is the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development.
- the ECOWAS court of justice: The court is the Community Court of Justice.
- the planned single currency of ECOWAS: The planned currency is the eco.

options.label: B
options.content: the ECOWAS ceasefire monitoring group (peacekeeping force)

options.label: D
options.content: the planned single currency of ECOWAS

questions.stem: The three countries that left ECOWAS in January 2025 were
questions.explanation:
After military coups, Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger formed the Alliance of Sahel States and left ECOWAS.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Mauritania, Senegal and The Gambia: Mauritania left in 2000; Senegal and The Gambia are members.
- Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone: These are members of both ECOWAS and the Mano River Union.
- Ghana, Togo and Benin: These remain ECOWAS members.

questions.stem: The Mano River Union was founded in 1973 by
questions.explanation:
The union is named after the Mano River on the Sierra Leone–Liberia border; its headquarters is in Freetown.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire: They joined later, in 1980 and 2008.
- Nigeria and Ghana: They are not Mano River Union members.
- Senegal and Mali: They are not Mano River Union members.

papers.title: Map Reading and Interpretation: practice set 1
papers.description: 5 original WASSCE-style objective questions on map reading and interpretation, each with an explanation and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: On a map with a scale of 1:50,000, 1 cm represents
questions.explanation:
1 cm represents 50,000 cm = 500 m = 0.5 km.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 5 km: 50,000 cm is 500 m, not 5 km.
- 50 km: That confuses centimetres with metres.
- 0.05 km: 50,000 cm is 0.5 km, not 0.05 km.

questions.stem: On a 1:50,000 map, a straight road measures 6 cm. Its length on the ground is
questions.explanation:
6 cm × 0.5 km = 3 km.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 30 km: Each centimetre is 0.5 km, not 5 km.
- 0.3 km: Each centimetre is 0.5 km, not 0.05 km.
- 12 km: That multiplies by 2 instead of dividing.

questions.stem: The bearing of a school from a church is 070°. The bearing of the church from the school is
questions.explanation:
Back bearing = 070° + 180° = 250°.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 110°: That subtracts the bearing from 180°.
- 290°: That subtracts the bearing from 360°.
- 070°: The return direction is the opposite one.

questions.stem: Contour lines that are very close together on a map show
questions.explanation:
Close contours mean a large change in height over a short distance.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a gentle slope: Widely spaced contours show a gentle slope.
- flat land: Flat land has few or no contours.
- a river valley floor: Valley floors are usually gently sloping.

questions.stem: Two places differ in height by 100 m and are 2 km apart. The average gradient between them is
questions.explanation:
Gradient = vertical interval ÷ horizontal equivalent = 100 m ÷ 2,000 m = 1/20, i.e. 1 in 20.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 1 in 2: The distance must be in metres: 2 km is 2,000 m.
- 1 in 200: 100 ÷ 2,000 is 1/20, not 1/200.
- 1 in 50: That divides 100 into 5,000 instead of 2,000.

papers.title: Geographical Field Work and Survey: practice set 1
papers.description: 5 original WASSCE-style objective questions on geographical field work and survey, each with an explanation and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: A first visit to a study area to check access, safety and what can be studied is called
questions.explanation:
Reconnaissance is an early planning step before the main fieldwork.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a census: A census counts a whole population.
- a traverse: A traverse is a series of survey lines.
- a questionnaire: A questionnaire is a list of written questions.

questions.stem: In a chain survey, offsets are measured
questions.explanation:
Each feature is fixed by its chainage along the line and its offset at a right angle.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- along the chain line from station to station: Distances along the line are chainages.
- as bearings from magnetic north: Bearings are used in compass survey.
- vertically to find heights: Heights are measured by levelling.

options.label: A
options.content: along the chain line from station to station

options.label: C
options.content: at right angles from the chain line to features

questions.stem: The instrument used to measure bearings in a traverse survey is the
questions.explanation:
The prismatic compass gives forward and back bearings at each station.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- ranging pole: Ranging poles mark stations and keep lines straight.
- rain gauge: A rain gauge measures rainfall.
- clinometer: A clinometer measures slope angles.

questions.stem: Choosing every tenth house along a street for an interview is an example of
questions.explanation:
Systematic sampling chooses items at regular intervals.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- random sampling: In random sampling every item has an equal chance, chosen without a pattern.
- stratified sampling: Stratified sampling divides the population into groups first.
- a census: A census includes every house.

questions.stem: Ranging poles are used in chain survey to
questions.explanation:
Lining up the ranging poles keeps the chain line straight between stations.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- measure the length of offsets: Offsets are measured with an offset staff or tape.
- measure the angle of a slope: Slopes are measured with a clinometer.
- record measurements: Measurements are recorded in a field book.

options.label: B
options.content: mark the stations and keep the chain line straight

options.label: C
options.content: measure the angle of a slope

papers.title: Statistical Geography: practice set 1
papers.description: 5 original WASSCE-style objective questions on statistical geography, each with an explanation and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: In a pie chart, a part worth 100 out of a total of 400 is shown by a sector of
questions.explanation:
Angle = 100 ÷ 400 × 360° = 90°.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 100°: The angle is not the raw value.
- 25°: 25 is the percentage, not the angle.
- 45°: That divides by 800 instead of 400.

questions.stem: Which graph is best for showing how the population of a town changed over twenty years?
questions.explanation:
Line graphs show trends in continuous data over time.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a pie chart: A pie chart shows parts of a whole at one time.
- a dot map: A dot map shows distribution in space, not change over time.
- a divided bar: A divided bar shows parts of a total.

questions.stem: Isohyets are lines on a map joining places with equal
questions.explanation:
Isohyets show how rainfall varies across an area.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- temperature: Lines of equal temperature are isotherms.
- pressure: Lines of equal pressure are isobars.
- height: Lines of equal height are contours.

questions.stem: A map on which areas are shaded darker for higher values, such as population density, is a
questions.explanation:
Choropleth maps shade each area by class, using shades of one colour.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- dot map: Dot maps use dots of a fixed value.
- flow map: Flow maps use arrows to show movement.
- isopleth map: Isopleth maps join points of equal value with lines.

questions.stem: The median of the values 4, 9, 2, 7 and 5 is
questions.explanation:
In order: 2, 4, 5, 7, 9. The middle value is 5.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 5.4: 5.4 is the mean (27 ÷ 5).
- 2: 2 is the middle value of the list before it is put in order.
- 7: 7 is the range (9 − 2).
